A few details about your home can help us
start with the questions that matter to you.
Hotter days can mean more air-conditioning use. Thermostat settings, equipment efficiency, and how long systems run all affect electricity use. Electric heating can also add to winter use.
We’ll ask: When does your usage rise, and how do you heat and cool your home?
The space you cool or heat, insulation, windows, and air leaks affect how much work your system needs to do to keep your home comfortable.
We’ll ask: About how large is your home, and are any rooms hard to keep comfortable?
Household size and time spent at home influence lighting, laundry, cooking, and cooling needs. Working from home can change when you use electricity.
We’ll ask: How many people live at home, and when is someone usually there?
Appliance efficiency and running time matter. Electric water heaters, dryers, pool pumps, and EV charging can contribute to use; gas appliances use a different fuel.
We’ll ask: What runs on electricity, and do you expect to add an EV or other equipment?
Electricity use and your bill aren’t the same thing.

Kilowatt-hours (kWh) measure electricity used; dollars measure what you pay. Rates, fees, and—if your plan has time-of-use pricing—when you use electricity can affect your bill. Solar generates electricity; it doesn’t automatically reduce how much your appliances use.
. These are general factors, not a home assessment or savings estimate.

We’re Group 9 in MGMT 3400. Our business idea is simple: help Bakersfield residents feel more informed about solar and take the next step toward exploring potential energy savings.
Through free consultations and installer referrals, we aim to make getting started feel more approachable. We provide guidance; installers handle technical assessments, quotes, and installation.
Here are a few things to know
Yes. Our business concept offers free initial consultations by phone or in person, so homeowners can ask questions before considering their next step.
Do you install the solar panels?

No. Kern Solar Connect is a consultation and referral concept. Solar installers would assess your home, provide quotes, and handle installation. No installer partnerships have been established for this class project.
How much could I save with solar?

There’s no single answer for every home. Potential savings depend on your energy use, system costs, roof conditions, utility rates, and other factors. An installer would need to assess your home and provide an estimate. Savings are not guaranteed.
